thesis: P&G's fiscal Q1 FY27 results (Oct 22) showed organic sales +4.0%, driven mostly by volume (+2.4%). All 10 categories and all six regions grew organically. The stock is about 1% below its 52-week high, and its 60-day move is +18%. The strongest counter-case is that management held full-year organic growth guidance at 1-3% and flagged rising oil and petrochemical costs in coming quarters. That suggests the strong quarter may not compound, and the run found no clear evidence that it doesn't. The run found no litigation with a scheduled date and no governance events.
invalidation: Q2 FY27 organic sales growth falls back toward the bottom of the 1-3% range, or management cuts core EPS guidance on input costs

thesis: SO is up about 10.7% over 60 days and sits about 6% below its 52-week high. This run found no company-specific catalyst for the move, which looks consistent with sector-wide utility strength rather than a disclosed company event. On Nov 10 a federal judge denied the motion to dismiss a 2022 ERISA pension class action. The case is open, but no ruling or trial date inside 90 days was found, so it isn't flagged. Kemper-era securities litigation was settled years ago, outside the 3-year governance window. With no identified catalyst, there is no clear net read beyond trend.
invalidation: Price breaks below the 200-day SMA, or the ERISA case moves to a scheduled trial or adverse ruling
sources: Southern Co ERISA ruling coverage (Cohen Milstein): https://www.cohenmilstein.com/southern-co-cant-toss-erisa-fight-11th-circ-revived/

thesis: Home Depot reported Q3 FY26 results on Nov 17. Sales were $43.4B (+4.9%), comps rose 2.2%, and adjusted EPS of $3.86 slightly beat the $3.84 estimate. The full-year sales outlook moved to the top of its range (~4.5%). However, adjusted EPS growth was pinned near ~2%, and operating margin guidance moved to the low end (~12.4%). Shares fell after the report. The setup suggests revenue strength isn't reaching earnings. The 60-day run-up of +16% leaves room for further de-rating. Richard McPhail was named incoming CEO alongside the release, which the sources present as planned succession rather than a for-cause exit. The counter-case is the sales beat and raised top-line outlook. The margin squeeze is the more decision-relevant signal for near-term price.
invalidation: Q4 guidance or housing data shows margin recovery, or shares reclaim pre-earnings levels on volume

thesis: SKHY is down about 35% over 60 days. That followed a sharp early-November selloff (about -23% in one week per TIKR) tied to US data-center regulation worries and Nvidia financing concerns. The Motley Fool also cited held-up US export licenses for equipment bound for SK hynix's China NAND plants. Against that, Q3 2026 results (Oct 28) were records, and more than half of 2027-28 capacity is reportedly contracted. The evidence is mixed, and the drop is largely sector and macro driven. Today's close at a 52-week low suggests the selling isn't exhausted. The 200-day trend check was skipped because the US listing has only 91 real daily bars.
invalidation: Price stabilizes and reclaims its 20-day average, or US export licenses for China plants are granted

thesis: SPCX is down about 10% over 60 days. Recent moves track the broad AI and tech tape: -9% on Nov 5 alongside a 5.5% Nasdaq drop, then +8.6% the next day with no company news. This is a sector-driven move. Company items are mixed. Q3 revenue was reported at $14.6B. Against that, AI campus spending could exceed $74B, EchoStar is reportedly due up to $35B in SpaceX stock, and a Starship test flight is pending. A Google executive left the board, which SpaceX said involved no disagreement. Sourcing is mostly secondary, and the read is unresolved. The 200-day trend check was skipped because there are only 109 real daily bars.
invalidation: Starship flight succeeds and price reclaims its pre-November range on volume, or a clear capex/funding plan reduces dilution concerns

thesis: CHYM traded 8.9x its 30-day average volume today. That coincides with its S&P MidCap 400 addition (replacing NorthWestern) effective Nov 18, which suggests the spike is largely mechanical index-rebalance flow rather than new fundamental information. The 60-day move is +13%. Underlying fundamentals are supportive. Q3 2026 revenue rose 32% to $718M, Chime swung to $43.7M net income, and the pending $590M cash acquisition of Stride Bank is expected to close in H1 2027. An April 2026 data-breach class action (N.D. Cal.) is open. Reports conflict on whether a settlement exists, and no scheduled ruling or hearing inside 90 days could be confirmed, so it isn't flagged. A 2024 CFPB consent order is resolved. Because the volume driver is mechanical, the read is low conviction.
invalidation: Post-inclusion selling pushes price back below the 200-day SMA, or the breach litigation produces a scheduled adverse ruling

thesis: BILL jumped about 13% to a 52-week high on 6.7x average volume. That followed a Financial Times report that a TPG-led consortium is nearing a take-private deal at a premium to the ~$4.8B market cap. Activists Elliott and Starboard are among the top holders. The catalyst is a report of advanced talks, not a signed agreement, and sources describe the talks as fluid and able to fall through. At today's price, upside appears capped near an undisclosed deal premium, while a collapse of talks would likely reverse the move. Earnings Whispers also lists a conflicting Nov 18 earnings date. The asymmetry argues against a new entry until terms are confirmed.
invalidation: A definitive merger agreement is announced with a price meaningfully above current levels (removes the downside-reversal risk)

thesis: HZN is the renamed Black Hills Corp. after its all-stock NorthWestern merger closed (8-K; NYSE trading as HZN began Nov 16). Today's 4.5x volume and -5.5% move coincide with NorthWestern holders receiving 0.98 HZN shares and NWE's S&P MidCap 400 deletion effective Nov 18. That suggests mechanical post-merger flow rather than new fundamental information. The 60-day +21% move largely reflects approvals, including Montana PSC (Nov 10), ahead of close. No litigation or governance items surfaced. With the catalyst now complete and current trading driven by index and holder churn, there is no clear entry thesis.
invalidation: Post-merger selling subsides and the combined company issues synergy/rate-base guidance that re-rates the stock

thesis: Held position. LIN is up about 13.7% over 60 days but is 6% below its 52-week high and slipped 1.6% today. The Q3 2026 results (Oct 29) were mixed. EPS was $3.66, down 11% and roughly in line with estimates, and guidance trailed consensus. Lincare headwinds were offset by electronics demand and a ~$2B project backlog. Linde also took a $425M restructuring charge, and Lincare is under strategic review. No litigation with scheduled dates or governance events surfaced. The only CFO resignation found was at the separate Linde India subsidiary. The evidence is mixed and the restructuring payoff is pushed to H2 2027, so there is no clear net read, but the trend remains above the 200-day SMA.
invalidation: Price breaks below the 200-day SMA, or Lincare review results in a dilutive or value-destructive outcome

thesis: Held position. Costco declared a $30/share special dividend (~$13.3B, record date Nov 24, payable Dec 4) and reauthorized a $4B buyback through 2030. These are confirmed, company-disclosed capital-return actions, and they pushed the stock to all-time highs. It is up 24% over 60 days and sits 1.2% below its Nov 17 52-week high. The strongest counter-evidence is valuation (P/E ~54). The special dividend will also mechanically lower the share price by about $30 at the Nov 24 ex-date. Even so, the payout is funded from accumulated cash and signals cash generation, and the ex-date adjustment is not a loss of value. The read doesn't change. Open tariff-refund class actions (Seattle, Illinois) have no scheduled hearing found, so they aren't flagged. The next binary event is Q1 FY27 earnings on Dec 10, after the next review.
invalidation: Q1 FY27 results on Dec 10 show comp deceleration or margin compression, or price breaks below its 50-day trend after the ex-dividend adjustment

thesis: Held position. Lilly's Q3 2026 results (Oct 29) are a confirmed company-disclosed catalyst. Revenue rose 39% to $24.4B, Mounjaro grew 65% to $10.7B and Zepbound 49%, and full-year revenue guidance was raised by $5.5B at the midpoint to $91-92B. The stock is up 24% over 60 days and sits 4% below its Nov 16 52-week high. The strongest counter-evidence is that non-GAAP EPS guidance was trimmed to $35-36. That trim comes from $4.2B of acquired IPR&D charges, while underlying EPS guidance rose $4.07 at the midpoint, so it doesn't change the read. The Streck False Claims Act judgment (~$184M, upheld Sept 2025) is immaterial at Lilly's scale and has no scheduled date found, so it isn't flagged. No binary event was found before the next review.
invalidation: Revenue guidance cut or GLP-1 pricing/volume deterioration disclosed, or price breaks below the 200-day SMA
